Oral Order
1

.  These petitions arise out of the same crime and are therefore taken up, heard, and disposed of by a common order.
2.

The petitioners, who have been charge-sheeted for offences punishable under Sections 323, 498A,
417, 504, and 506 read with Section 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, are before this Court seeking relief.
3. The prosecution alleges that Accused No.1 is the husband of the defacto-complainant and that their marriage was solemnized on 15.10.2021.
After the marriage, the defacto-complainant resided in the NC: 2025:KHC:15006 matrimonial home for a period of 25 to 30 days.

Thereafter, she was forced to leave and started residing at her parental home in Tumakuru due to harassment allegedly caused by petitioner-Accused No.1 (husband) and Accused Nos.2 and 3 (parents-in-law).
Accused No.1 is said to be insisting that the defacto-complainant consent to mutually dissolve the marriage and is refusing to take her back to the matrimonial home to lead a cordial marital life.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the charge sheet material indicates that the defacto-complainant resided in the matrimonial home for only 25 to 30 days.

The allegations against Accused Nos.2 and 3 are omnibus and general in nature, with no specific overt act detailing how and in what manner they allegedly subjected the defacto-complainant to mental or physical cruelty or demanded money from her parental home.

The allegations against Accused No.1, however, are specific, and the veracity of such allegations can be assessed during the trial; such an assessment is not appropriate at this stage of the proceedings.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar, has held at paragraph 18 as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others vs. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this Court has, on numerous occasions, expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498A IPC and the increasing tendency to implicate relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes without analyzing the long-term ramifications of a trial on both the complainant and the accused.

It is further evident from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations, made in the course of matrimonial disputes, if left unchecked, would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this Court,
through its judgments, has cautioned the courts against proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
7.

Therefore, in the absence of any specific overt act attributed to Accused Nos.2 and 3, the continuation of criminal proceedings based solely on omnibus and general allegations would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
The trial court cannot frame charges against Accused Nos.2 and 3 solely on the basis of such vague allegations.

8. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The Criminal petition No.563/2024 is allowed.
The Criminal petition No.1000/2024
is dismissed.
iii. The impugned proceedings in CC.No.447/2023 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge, JMFC Court, Tumakuru in so far as accused Nos.2 and 3 is hereby quashed.

sentences.text: iv. The trial Court, to proceed against the accused No.1 in accordance with law.

As against accused No.1 no observation is made in this order and observation made in this order is only in relation to accused Nos.2 and 3.
v.
All the contentions of the parties before the trial Court are kept open.
